summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures, including one hour of debate and a motion to recommit, for considering two Senate resolutions to block CFPB rules on overdraft lending and digital payments plus bills limiting federal court injunctions and requiring citizenship proof to register for federal elections.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural and facilitates consideration of CFPB rule disapprovals and judicial/voting bills. None of these directly address government spending levels or budgets.
No provisions or facilitated bills relate to tax rates, revenue, or tax policy.
No connection to healthcare coverage, markets, or policy.
No engagement with firearms regulations or rights.
No provisions touching immigration pathways or enforcement.
No relation to abortion access or restrictions.
No military or defense spending elements.
No environmental regulations or protections addressed.
No welfare, benefits, or safety net programs involved.
No education funding, schools, or choice provisions.
No drug enforcement or decriminalization measures.
H.R. 1526 limits injunctive relief by courts but does not address sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation directly.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization content.
No deficit, debt reduction, or fiscal policy elements.
No LGBTQ+ protections or limitations discussed.
No foreign aid provisions.

Section 4 explicitly sets rules for considering H.R. 22, which amends voter registration law to require proof of U.S. citizenship. This directly facilitates a bill advancing stricter election integrity measures.
S.J. Res. 28 concerns a CFPB rule on digital payment applications, but the resolution itself only provides procedural consideration and does not engage substantively with tech regulation or privacy.
No labor, union, or worker protection content.
No religious liberty or anti-discrimination provisions.
